before: TypeScript usually compares object structure: a named value with the required fields can fit a smaller object type. Having extra fields is not the same as having a wrong required field.

Complete greet(guest). Guest needs a name:string. Return "Hello, " followed by that name. A named object may also carry other fields; do not delete or change them. The function only needs the name, and it does not validate outside data.
after: TypeScript usually compares objects by their structure. A named object can fit a smaller type if it has the required fields with the right types. Extra fields do not automatically make those required fields wrong.
Passing visitor does not remove visits. The function reads the name and leaves the object unchanged.

A fresh object written directly in the call gets an extra-property check. Including visits directly in a call expecting only PersonName would be rejected here. Naming an object first still does not make a wrong required value, such as name: 3, acceptable.
Make Guest require a string name. Make greet return Hello, followed by a space and that name. Leave all fields of the supplied object unchanged.
